Create a policy to define an ordered chain of provider/model targets. Reference it per-request via X-LLM-Fallback-Policy-Id — fallback never applies automatically.
Create policy
What are Fallback Policies?
A fallback policy is an ordered chain of (provider, model) targets. When a request fails on the primary target with a configured trigger error, the router transparently retries on the next hop — without the client seeing any failure. Fallback is opt-in per request via a header.
Read the docs
Define a chain
Pick an ordered list of (provider, model) pairs — up to 8. The first is your primary; the rest are fallback hops.
Set trigger conditions
Choose which error classes advance to the next hop — rate limits, timeouts, server errors. Request-attributable errors never trigger by default.
Reference per request
Opt in via header: X-LLM-Fallback-Policy-Id: your-id. No header = no fallback. No auto-apply, ever.

Eval Suites
Each suite groups a set of test cases around a single use-case or system prompt. Click a suite to manage its test cases and run evaluations.
New Suite
No eval suites yet
Create your first suite to get started. You'll be taken straight to the suite detail page where you can add test cases and run your first evaluation.
New Suite
What is EvalLab?
EvalLab lets you systematically test your prompts against multiple LLM models at once and automatically score the results — so you can pick the right model based on real data, not guesswork. Define what a good response looks like, run the evaluation, and get a data-driven routing recommendation you can apply with one click.
Create a suite
Name your eval, set an optional system prompt, and choose a quality floor — the minimum score a model must hit to be recommended.
Add test cases
Write the messages you want to send and define how to score each response: exact match, substring check, regex, or an LLM judge with a custom rubric.
Run & apply
Select the models to compare, pick a sample size, and run. EvalLab scores every response and recommends the cheapest model that meets your quality floor.

What are Prompts?
Prompts let you store reusable system prompts centrally and inject them into any LLM request via a single header — so you can manage tone, context, and instructions in one place without hard-coding them into your application.
Create a prompt
Give your prompt a title, write the system instructions, and toggle it on or off whenever you need.
Attach via header
Pass the x-prompt-id header in your API request and the stored system prompt is injected automatically.
Iterate & manage
Edit wording, enable or disable prompts instantly, and keep every variation in one place — no code deploys required.

New Rule
What are Guardrails?
Guardrails are project-level rules that validate, mask, or block model inputs and outputs at the gateway. Define a rule once and every chat completion in this project is checked automatically — no application-side validation needed.
Read the docs
Pick a direction
Input checks user prompts before they reach the model. Output checks model responses before they reach the user.
Choose a mode
Regex, string presence, JSON Schema, or LLM judge. Each runs against the serialized payload with strict performance budgets.
Set an action
Reject blocks the request, mask rewrites matched spans, log only is dry-run for monitoring before you turn enforcement on.
